At 3.00 p.m. 8/8/32, D.S. Moore accompanied by C.D.C's Mo Zau Woo
and Foo Tseu Zung attached to the Bureau of Public Safety, came
to the station and requested assistance in arresting one Wong
Kyung San (王金山) who was reported to be residing at 104 Tan
Oen Li, Tong Dong Ka Loong, and to be engaged in Communistic
activities. A visit was paid to the given address but it was
found that the man was absent but that he habitually returned in
the early hours of the morning.
At 5.50 a.m. 9/8/32, the above mentioned C.D.Cs
again came to the station unaccompanied by any representative of
the S.M.P. and stated that Det. Inspector Ross had instructed them
to return to the station at this time to again attempt to effect
the arrest. When questioned as to the absence of a warrant, they
further stated that D.I. Ross had waived the matter and had told
them to proceed without a warrant. Upon this understanding, the
undersigned and C.D.C's 284 and 297 accompanied the repres-
entatives of the P.S.B. to 104 Tong Dong Ka Loong and there
arrested Wong Kyung San (王金山). He was taken to West Hongkew
station as was a small quantity of Communistic literature found
among his effects, and D.S. Moore was communicated with and it was
then learned that after the fruitless visit to the above address
on 8/8/32, D.I. Ross instructed the detectives from the P.S.B. to
obtain warrants for the arrest of this man and the search of the
room occupied by him before again attempting the arrest.
The arrested man was questioned at the station and
admitted participation in the propagation of the Communist doctrine
and to having acted as a distributing agent for inflammatory
literature, he also made a statement to this effect.

The following is the statement of Wong Kyung San (王金山).
native of Anhwei taken by me D.P. S. Warman.
translated
at W. H'kew on the 9-8-32. and interpreted by Interpreter Chu,

My name is Wong Kyung San, native of Toong Lieu City,
Anhwei, age 24, male and residing at 104 Tai An Li off Tong Dong
Ka Loong.

During the month of July 1930 I came Shanghai from
Anhwei and have resided in the International Settlement for
about 7 months, at present I am unemployed, I can read and
write, I studied in the private school in Anhwei between the age
of 9 and 13, later I studied in the primary school, Anhwei until
I was age 17, since then I studied in the Anhwei Middle School,
Anhwei until I was age 21, after I had graduated in this school,
when I was 22 years of age I came Shanghai and studied in the
Law College, Kiangwan Road, I left there during the month of
June 1931. I have never been employed in any business, One day
during the month of March and April 1931 while I was in the
Hongkew Park, there came one man named Li who asked me to par-
ticipate in the communistic party, at that time I did not pro-
mise him to do so, later I again went to the Hongkew Park for
amusement on several occasions, this man again asked me to par-
ticipate in the communistic party, later I promised him, but I
did not receive any remuneration from the communistic party, I
performed my work for the distribution of the pamphlets. The
pamphlets, which were seized in my home, were delivered to me
by one named Woo on 26th July, when he gave me the pamphlets,
and he told me to distribute them. I have no relatives or
friends in Shanghai, and I have not been previously charged.
About one year ago, by the introduction of Li in the Hongkew
Park I became acquainted with one named Woo, after which

The following is the statement of Wong Kyung San (王金山),
native of Anhwei taken by me D.P.S. Harman.
translated
at Wo H'kew on the 9-8-32. and interpreted by Interpreter Chiu.

My name is Wong Kyung San, I was born and lived in native
of Toong Lieu City, Anhwei, age 24, male and residing at 104 Tai
An Li off Tong Dong Ka Loong.

I studied in the private school in Anhwei between the age
of 9 and 13, later I studied in the primary school, Anhwei until
I was age 17, since then I studied in the Anhwei Middle School,
Anhwei until I was age 22, after I had graduated in this school,
when I was 22 years of age I came Shanghai and studied in the
Law College, Kiangnan Road.

After living and studying in the village of Toong Lieu,
Anhwei until I reached the age of 22, I came to Shanghai to
study at the Law School, Kiangnan, arriving in Shanghai during
July 1930. I studied in this school until April 1931 without
engaging in any anti-government propaganda but during the month
of April 1931 I met in Hongkew Park, a man named Lee (李),
This man induced me to assist in the distribution of inflamma-
tory literature amongst the students of the school. This was
carried
/on until June 1931 when I left the Law School and went to live
at a house in Chapel at the rear of North Szechuen Road near
Juken Road, where I resided until December 1931 and then removed
to 14 Peiho Road and resided at this address until 22nd July
1932 when I removed to 104 Tung Dong Ka Loong at which place I
was arrested.

I was visited from time to time, usually at weekly inter-
vals, by one named Woo who brought certain pamphlets and gave me
instructions for their disposal, these visits usually took place
between 8.00 and 10.00 p.m. and lasted about 15 minutes. The

本人姓名王金山，出生于安徽桐庐市（Toong Lieu City，音译）并在此居住，年龄 24 岁，男性，现居住于通东卡龙路（Tong Dong Ka Loong，音译）泰安里 104 号。

本人 9 至 13 岁期间在安徽私塾读书，随后在安徽小学就读至 17 岁，此后在安徽中学就读至 22 岁，从该校毕业后，22 岁时来到上海，在江南路法学院求学。

在安徽桐庐村生活和学习直至 22 岁后，本人来到上海进入江南法学院学习，于 1930 年 7 月抵达上海。本人在该校学习直至 1931 年 4 月，期间未参与任何反政府宣传，但在 1931 年 4 月间，本人在虹口公园遇见一名姓李（Lee）的男子，该男子诱使本人协助在学校学生中分发煽动性刊物。此项工作一直持续
/到 1931 年 6 月，当时本人离开法学院，搬至北四川路近巨肯路（Juken Road，音译）后方查佩尔（Chapel，音译）的一处房屋居住，在此居住至 1931 年 12 月，随后迁至北河南路 14 号，并在此地址居住至 1932 年 7 月 22 日，当日迁至通东卡龙路 104 号，并在该处被捕。

一名姓吴的男子不时来访，通常每周一次，带来某些传单并指示本人如何处理，这些拜访通常发生在晚上 8:00 至 10:00 之间，持续约 15 分钟。

本人将收到的传单予以分发，通常在晚上 10:00 至午夜之间，在福建路桥附近区域进行分发。本人经常在午餐时间于南京路与四川路路口会见吴，以接受指示。本人从未因向共产党提供服务而收取任何报酬，且自离校以来，本人依靠父亲从安徽寄来的每月 30.00 元津贴维持生活，父亲至今仍以为本人是法学院的学生。

除了在法学院向学生分发传单外，本人未参与租界以外的共产主义活动，即使居住在闸北期间也是如此。本人总是在北四川路与兰路（Range Roads，音译）路口分发传单。

自离开法学院后，本人未受雇于任何商号，除吴和李之外，本人在上海不认识其他人，本人不知吴交给本人的传单是在何处或由何人印刷及递送，本人也不知这两人的住址。此乃本人真实供词。
